before: We matched the original macrophage annotations to refined immune annotations using nucleus barcodes. Composition summaries retained nuclei with unmatched labels and those reassigned to other categories. We represented donor composition using centred log ratios [44] and added its first two principal components to the model containing age and centre. We also reaggregated raw counts for all 20 CIDP and CIAP donors under alternative macrophage definitions. Tests of refined subtypes required at least 20 nuclei per donor and at least three eligible donors in each diagnosis group. Multiple testing correction covered the nine eligible refined subtypes.

after: In a focused exploratory follow up, we reconstructed the original 11 gene macrophage score using the same standardisation across all 37 atlas donors and compared CIDP and CIAP separately with the four graft reference donors. The CIDP versus reference comparison was present in the original pipeline and was reexamined here. Two sided exact Mann and Whitney tests were corrected across the two reference comparisons. We also added these comparisons to the 89 module and programme tests as a 91 test sensitivity family. Mean difference intervals used 20,000 donor bootstrap replicates with independent resampling within each group, fixed score standardisation and seed 20260921. These comparisons contextualised the primary contrast within the same cohort.

before: The macrophage Fc receptor module showed the strongest statistical evidence of a difference between CIDP and CIAP, with a mean score difference of −0.673 (CIDP minus CIAP, P = 0.0011). Its q value was 0.0087 across eight macrophage modules, 0.087 across the original 80 nerve module tests and 0.097 after adding the nine functional programme contrasts to that family. Macrophage leukocyte transmigration and macrophage state scores were also lower, with differences of −0.345 (P = 0.0185, q = 0.074) and −0.368 (P = 0.0334, q = 0.089), respectively. The original endothelial BNB identity score was lower by 0.404 (P = 0.0276, q = 0.221). These latter q values refer to eight modules within the corresponding cell group (Fig. 4B).

after: Comparison with the four graft reference donors did not establish a difference for either diagnosis. The mean Fc score difference was −0.401 for CIDP versus reference (bootstrap 95% confidence interval −0.901 to 0.050, exact P = 0.330) and 0.271 for CIAP versus reference (−0.171 to 0.652, exact P = 0.343). Both comparisons had q = 0.343 across the two reference tests. All reference donors came from one centre, and only one was male. The intervals were wide, so these results do not establish equivalent expression or a normal reference level.

before: None of the nine separated endothelial and Schwann cell programme contrasts passed correction within the new nine test family or across all 89 nerve module and programme tests. The endothelial transport score was lower in CIDP by 0.593 (P = 0.0276, q = 0.248 across nine tests and q = 0.425 across 89 tests). Its age and centre adjusted difference was −0.615 (95% confidence interval −1.448 to 0.217, P = 0.136). Junction and adhesion scores had unadjusted q values of 0.939. Neither the myelin maintenance nor injury response score differed after correction in any of the three Schwann cell groups. Adjustment for age, centre and the repair cell fraction in the pooled repair and damage group did not yield a significant disease contrast (Fig. 5A and B).

before: Within the original analysis of nerve cell groups, the macrophage Fc receptor module showed the strongest statistical evidence of a difference between CIDP and CIAP. The estimated difference remained negative after demographic adjustment and omission analyses, with four receptor or signalling genes contributing to the lower score. Attenuation after composition adjustment indicates that the estimate is sensitive to how macrophage populations are represented in the model, an issue relevant to the diverse macrophage states described in the source atlas [27]. Published findings of complement deposition on endoneurial capillaries and altered peripheral B cell and CD8 effector profiles in CIDP provide broader context for immune involvement at different anatomical sites [29,37]. The lower Fc receptor score therefore characterises this particular comparison with CIAP, with its interpretation depending on macrophage composition and the scope of multiple testing correction.
after: The nerve result identifies a macrophage expression difference between CIDP and CIAP, but its direction relative to a nondiseased reference remains uncertain. The Fc receptor score remained lower in CIDP after demographic adjustment and omission analyses, with four receptor or signalling genes contributing to the contrast. Neither diagnosis showed a clear difference from the small graft reference group. Attenuation after composition adjustment shows that the estimate depends on how macrophage populations are represented, but does not distinguish a shift in cell proportions from altered expression within a cell state. Sparse refined subtypes prevented direct standardisation across the full disease cohort. This uncertainty makes macrophage state and tissue context central to interpreting the finding [27]. Published complement deposition on endoneurial capillaries and altered peripheral B cell and CD8 effector profiles provide broader context for immune involvement [29,37]. They measure different endpoints and do not validate the Fc receptor contrast.

before: The nerve comparison involved nine CIDP and 11 CIAP donors and cannot define disease changes relative to healthy nerve. All CIDP donors were male, recruitment was uneven across centres, and treatment or other clinical factors may have influenced expression. The Fc receptor result did not survive correction across the original 80 or expanded 89 nerve tests and attenuated after composition adjustment. Functional gene sets and clinical extensions were added after inspecting the original findings. Their separate and expanded testing families describe exploratory evidence and do not turn the analysis into a confirmatory study. Small samples, correlated tests and selective prior attention to the original modules remain limitations.
after: The primary nerve comparison involved nine CIDP and 11 CIAP donors. The four graft reference donors were few, came from one centre and differed in sex distribution, limiting estimation of disease changes relative to reference nerve. All CIDP donors were male, and treatment or other clinical factors may have influenced expression. The Fc receptor result did not survive correction in the expanded nerve testing family and attenuated after composition adjustment. Functional gene sets and clinical and reference extensions were examined after the original findings were known. Their separate and expanded testing families describe exploratory evidence. Small samples, correlated tests and selective prior attention to the original modules remain limitations.

before: Blood, CSF and nerve samples came from separate participants, with diagnosis partly linked to specimen type. These data cannot establish a cross tissue pathological sequence or progression from GBS to CIDP. No independent disease matched nerve cohort replicated the Fc receptor or separated programme findings. The normal BNB reference is anatomical evidence, published complement observations concern a different endpoint, and the companion spatial panel contains none of the specified Fc receptor module genes. Internal resampling, covariate adjustment and alternative annotations assess sensitivity within the source cohort. Paired specimens, independent nerve cohorts and functional experiments are needed to test mechanistic connections.
after: Blood, CSF and nerve samples came from separate participants, with diagnosis partly linked to specimen type. These data cannot establish a cross tissue pathological sequence or progression from GBS to CIDP. No independent disease matched nerve cohort replicated the Fc receptor or separated programme findings. The normal BNB reference is anatomical evidence, published complement observations concern a different endpoint, and the companion spatial panel contains none of the specified Fc receptor module genes. The inspected PXD056286 database listed 19 instrument runs and protein abundance fields, but its sample group, replicate group and study factor fields did not provide a diagnosis mapping. We therefore did not estimate protein disease contrasts from those runs. Internal resampling, covariate adjustment, reference comparisons and alternative annotations assess sensitivity within the source cohort. Paired specimens, independent nerve cohorts and functional experiments are needed to test mechanistic connections.
